relevance_note: Case report of two patients with GFAP variants: "two de novo mutations in the glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) gene (c.214G>A and c.1235C>T) were identified in unrelated patients".
method_note: Read the paper in full; rows written by hand into a Python builder script in scratch and every span checked verbatim against the Markdown by script. In scope: probands P3433 and P4288, plus the five AxD post-mortem brain donors listed in supplementary Table SI (GEO GSE116327, ref 21) with sex, age and diagnosis; these are labelled 'Table SI #<NIH ID>' (bare-number ID column) and carry source_reference_in_review = the dataset citation; their Age column has no unit, so no ISO value was given; vital status 'deceased' comes from 'post-mortem human brain samples'. The three healthy-control donors, 500 genetic controls and 15 imaging controls are out of scope. Transcript NM_002055.5 is from the paper's statement that all GFAP variants were denoted as RefSeq NM_002055.5; no protein notation is printed for either variant, and the variant type is not stated (left 'not reported'). Zygosity is not stated for either patient. Contradiction: the Functional analysis section twice writes 'c.1235G>T' while everywhere else the variant is 'c.1235C>T'; spans for P4288's functional evidence were taken from the c.1235C>T mentions only. P4288 'Laboratory investigations were almost normal' was not recorded as an exclusion (hedged). P3433 'Laboratory examinations yielded unremarkable findings' is recorded as written ('abnormal laboratory examinations' excluded), excluding nothing more specific. P4288 'speech disfluency' was not mapped to the checklist item 'dysarthria or dysphonia' (left not reported). P4288 thoracic spinal cord thinning is not cervical cord/medulla; the medulla checklist item for P4288 rests on the Discussion statement naming the two patients. Pathological reflexes were mapped to 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' and positive finger-to-nose / poor coordination to 'ataxia or cerebellar signs'. Grey matter atrophy of putamen and thalamus (voxel-based morphometry vs controls) was mapped to 'basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality' for P3433; P4288's 'no significant grey matter differences' was not used to exclude that broader item. No ages at diagnosis are stated. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say its probands were described before.
